hints: For n = 19 Cheetahs, the median position is (19 + 1) / 2 = 10th value.
Read the 10th value from the stem-and-leaf diagram: median = 99 minutes.
The lower quartile Q1 is the 5th value (83), and the upper quartile Q3 is the 15th value (106).
walkthrough:
Determine the position of the median for $n = 19$ Cheetahs:
$$\text{Position of median } Q_2 = \frac{19 + 1}{2} = 10\text{th value}$$
$$\text{Median} = 99\text{ minutes}$$

Find the positions and values of the lower and upper quartiles:
$$\text{Position of } Q_1 = \frac{19 + 1}{4} = 5\text{th value} = 83\text{ minutes}$$
$$\text{Position of } Q_3 = 3 \times 5 = 15\text{th value} = 106\text{ minutes}$$

Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 106 - 83 = 23\text{ minutes}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Medians and Quartiles: Identifies median = 99, Q1 = 83, Q3 = 106, and calculates IQR = 23.

teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Count the total number of Cheetahs: $n = 19$.

Step 2: Find the rank of the median:
$$\text{Rank of median} = \frac{n + 1}{2} = \frac{19 + 1}{2} = 10$$
Counting to the 10th leaf for Cheetahs gives:
$$\text{Median} = 99\text{ minutes}$$

Step 3: Find the ranks of the lower and upper quartiles:
$$\text{Rank of } Q_1 = \frac{n + 1}{4} = \frac{20}{4} = 5$$
Reading the 5th value gives $Q_1 = 83$ minutes.
$$\text{Rank of } Q_3 = \frac{3(n + 1)}{4} = \frac{3 \times 20}{4} = 15$$
Reading the 15th value gives $Q_3 = 106$ minutes.

Step 4: Compute the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 106 - 83 = 23\text{ minutes}$$

hints: Compare the measure of central tendency: Cheetahs median (99) versus Panthers median (103).
Compare the measure of spread: Cheetahs IQR (23) versus Panthers IQR (14).
Make both statements clearly in the context of the race times.
walkthrough:
Compare central tendency in context:
$$\text{Median(Cheetahs)} = 99 < 103 = \text{Median(Panthers)}$$
$$\text{On average, the Cheetahs were faster than the Panthers (lower median completion time).}$$

Compare spread in context:
$$\operatorname{IQR}(\text{Cheetahs}) = 23 > 14 = \operatorname{IQR}(\text{Panthers})$$
$$\text{The times of the Cheetahs are more spread out (more varied) than the times of the Panthers.}$$

ai_rubric.Comparing Distributions: Compares medians (Cheetahs faster on average) and IQRs (Cheetahs times more spread out) in context.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the two aspects required for comparing distributions:
1. A comparison of location / central tendency (using the medians).
2. A comparison of spread / dispersion (using the interquartile ranges).

Step 2: Compare medians:
- Cheetahs median $= 99$ minutes
- Panthers median $= 103$ minutes
Since a lower time indicates a faster race, on average the Cheetahs were faster than the Panthers.

Step 3: Compare interquartile ranges:
- Cheetahs IQR $= 23$ minutes
- Panthers IQR $= 14$ minutes
The Cheetahs have a higher IQR, which means their times have greater variation and are more spread out than the Panthers.

skill_tags: Calculating a Mean from Raw Data

hints: With Kenny added, there are 20 Cheetahs and their mean time is 99 minutes.
Calculate the total time for all 20 Cheetahs: 20 * 99 = 1980 minutes.
Sum the times of the original 19 Cheetahs from the stem-and-leaf diagram: total = 1862 minutes.
Subtract to find Kenny's time: 1980 - 1862 = 118 minutes.
walkthrough:
Find the total time for all 20 Cheetahs using the new mean:
$$\text{Total time for 20 Cheetahs} = 20 \times 99 = 1980\text{ minutes}$$

Sum the individual times of the original 19 Cheetahs from the stem-and-leaf diagram:
$$\sum x_{19} = 1862\text{ minutes}$$

Subtract the sum of the 19 times from the total of 20 times to find Kenny's time:
$$\text{Kenny's time} = 1980 - 1862 = 118\text{ minutes}$$

ai_rubric.Calculating a Mean from Raw Data: Finds total for 20 as 1980 and subtracts 1862 to find Kenny's time = 118 minutes.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Use the mean formula $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x}{n}$ to determine the new total sum of times:
With Kenny added, the number of Cheetahs is $n = 20$, and their mean time is $99$ minutes.
$$\text{Total time for 20 Cheetahs} = 20 \times 99 = 1980\text{ minutes}$$

Step 2: Sum the times of the original 19 Cheetahs from the stem-and-leaf diagram:
Adding all 19 values gives:
$$\sum x_{\text{original}} = 1862\text{ minutes}$$

Step 3: Set up the equation for Kenny's time $k$:
$$\frac{1862 + k}{20} = 99$$
$$1862 + k = 1980$$
$$k = 1980 - 1862 = 118\text{ minutes}$$
(This is equivalent to 1 hour 58 minutes.)
